```{r}
#| label: tokenization-comparison-data
#| include: false
token_rows <- read.csv("../lab/toy/tokenization_th_ja_zh_tokens.csv", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
thai_tokens <- token_rows$token[token_rows$language == "Thai"]
with_pos <- function(language) {
  rows <- token_rows[token_rows$language == language, ]
  paste0(rows$token, " (", rows$upos, ")")
}
thai_labels <- with_pos("Thai")
japanese_labels <- with_pos("Japanese")
chinese_labels <- with_pos("Chinese")
thai_provenance <- jsonlite::fromJSON("../lab/toy/udpipe_thai_provenance.json")
stopifnot(all(token_rows$method[token_rows$language == "Thai"] == "R httr2 / UDPipe 2 API"))
```

## Word tokenization across languages {.three-languages .pos-labels}

Straka & Straková (2017); Straka (2018)
:::

::: {.notes}
**Purpose.** Make word boundaries visible across Thai, Japanese, and Traditional Chinese.

**Explain.** Read the coffee sentences and then their tokens. Parentheses contain actual model POS predictions. The Japanese example has six displayed tokens; Thai and Chinese have three. Counts exclude punctuation and reflect these particular models and sentences.

**Ask.** Does a larger token count imply more information or stronger preference? No; segmentation conventions and grammatical expression differ.

**Transition.** Keep the coffee meaning but add grammatical relationships. The next slide replaces Japanese with English to provide a familiar reference alongside Chinese and Thai.

**Background and sources.**

Parenthesized labels are the models' actual universal POS (UPOS) predictions. PRON = pronoun, VERB = verb, NOUN = noun, ADP = adposition, ADJ = adjective, and AUX = auxiliary. Keep the Japanese model's ADP tags for は and が, and ADJ for 好き. These are model annotations, not manually assigned labels. Read the Japanese tokens left to right across each row, then continue to the next row.

All example scripts are R. Thai uses httr2 to call the official UDPipe 2 REST API with the pinned thai-tud-ud-2.17-251125 model. The cached API example was retrieved on `r substr(thai_provenance$retrieved_at, 1, 10)` (Asia/Taipei). udpipe_thai_api.R reuses the supplied raw JSON response by default, including its model and license metadata. It makes a request only when the cache is missing or the user explicitly requests `--refresh`. The remote service returned ฉัน/PRON, ชอบ/VERB and กาแฟ/NOUN. This model supplies no lemmas, represented by underscores in CoNLL-U. R udpipe_download_model() does not list Thai in its built-in catalogue. This does not mean UDPipe has no Thai model.

Japanese and Traditional Chinese run locally with udpipe::udpipe_annotate(parser = "none") and the japanese-gsd and chinese-gsd UD 2.5-191206 models. PUNCT tokens are excluded from displayed counts. This comparison illustrates particular language/model combinations, rather than a pure language effect under one identical model. The sentences are synthetic parallel examples. A fresh Thai request requires network access. The saved response supports offline rendering.

Sources: [UDPipe 2 models](https://ufal.mff.cuni.cz/udpipe/2/models), [official API client and endpoint](https://github.com/ufal/udpipe/blob/udpipe-2/udpipe2_client.py), [R udpipe guide](https://bnosac.github.io/udpipe/docs/doc2.html), [UDPipe 1 models](https://ufal.mff.cuni.cz/udpipe/1/models). Thai model license: CC BY-NC-SA, preserved in ../lab/toy/udpipe_thai_response.json.

Paper references: Straka, Milan, and Jana Straková. 2017. [Tokenizing, POS Tagging, Lemmatizing and Parsing UD 2.0 with UDPipe](https://aclanthology.org/K17-3009/). In *Proceedings of the CoNLL 2017 Shared Task: Multilingual Parsing from Raw Text to Universal Dependencies*, 88–99. Association for Computational Linguistics. doi:10.18653/v1/K17-3009.

Straka, Milan. 2018. [UDPipe 2.0 Prototype at CoNLL 2018 UD Shared Task](https://aclanthology.org/K18-2020/). In *Proceedings of the CoNLL 2018 Shared Task: Multilingual Parsing from Raw Text to Universal Dependencies*, 197–207. Association for Computational Linguistics. doi:10.18653/v1/K18-2020. These papers describe the software methods. The model versions and actual response provenance are documented above.
:::
